_comment: Pinned target+draft pair. This is NOT a free experimental variable: PROJECT.md fixes the model so that request-level acceptance heterogeneity is measured rather than model novelty. Checkpoints are SGLang's own canonical EAGLE3 test defaults (python/sglang/test/test_utils.py:114-115), so the configuration is known-good upstream.

launches.description: Absolute target-only baseline. No draft model, no speculation.
Static K=5. Present because 5 is in the default adaptive ladder, so it is an adaptive target tier.
Merged SGLang adaptive controller with the built-in default ladder ([1,3,5,7] at BS>=1). Initial steps 3 is a member of the ladder, so the slot keeps it rather than snapping to a midpoint.

_hardware_note.reasoning: Llama-3.1-8B fp16 is ~16.1 GB of weights plus ~1.5 GB for the EAGLE3 draft. At mem_fraction_static 0.7 a 24 GB card reserves only 16.8 GB total, which is less than the static weights alone, so startup OOMs before any KV cache is allocated. 48 GB (L40S / A6000) leaves ~16 GB for KV cache and the per-tier CUDA graphs.
smaller_gpu_options: Lower mem_fraction_static is NOT a fix: the weights are weights.
Quantized target (e.g. AWQ-INT4) would fit 24 GB but changes acceptance behaviour and adds a confounder -- use only as an explicitly-labelled secondary check, never as the primary pair.
Reduce cuda_graph_max_bs_decode to 32 to cut graph memory if VRAM is tight.
